properties.areaDesc: Petersburg Borough; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; Prince of Wales Island; City and Borough of Wrangell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 14 at 9:57PM AKDT until October 16 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger atmospheric river is expected to move over the panhandle
beginning early Thursday morning, continuing through Friday morning.
Multiple waves moving up will bring persistent moderate to heavy rain
for much of the southern half of the panhandle. Elevated gusty winds
are expected alongside this heavier rainfall on Thursday, with the
strongest winds expected Thursday night. Prolonged periods of
moderate to heavy rain will produce significant river rises with the
potential for at least minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Central Inner Channels, Southern Inner
Channels and Southeast Gulf Coast. This includes the cities of
Petersburg, Kake, Port Alexander, Craig, Klawock, Hydaburg, Coffman
Cove, Thorne Bay, And Wrangell.

* WHEN...From Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.
Street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
Isolated landslides are possible in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rain totals between early Thursday morning and late Friday
morning for the Central Panhandle and Prince of Wales Island area
are still expected to be around 2 to 3.5 inches, with higher rain
totals favoring southern facing mountain sides. Highest rain
rates are currently expected during the late morning through
evening timeframe on Thursday, where rates could be as high as
0.25 inches per hour.

Confidence has increased for the area seeing winds of 20 to 30
mph with gusts to 40 mph on Thursday, with potential for up to 50
mph wind gusts Thursday evening into the night. With the multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall and the elevated winds
Thursday, there is possibility for isolated landslides along
steep mountain slopes.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 12:50AM CDT until October 15 at 3:45AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Brewster County in southwestern Texas...

* Until 345 AM CDT.

* At 1250 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Castolon, Chisos Basin, Study Butte, Terlingua and Big Bend
National Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Typhoon Watch issued October 15 at 3:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...A TYPHOON WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FOR THE MARIANAS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Watch continues for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan in the
Mariana Islands.

A Typhoon Watch means that Typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or greater, are possible within the next 48 hours somewhere
within the specified areas.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 1 PM ChST...the center of Tropical Depression 29W was located
near latitude 10.8N...longitude 158.9E. This was about 970 miles
east of Guam. Storm motion was west-northwest, 285 degrees, at
13 mph. 29W is expected to make a turn toward the west over the next
couple of days. Storm intensity was 35 mph. 29W is expected to begin
to intensify Friday.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
It is vital that you do not focus on the exact forecast track. To
do so could result in bad decisions and place you or those you
are responsible for at greater risk. Tropical Depression 29W is
currently moving west-northwest, but is expected to make a turn
toward the west through this evening. It is too early to provide
exact wind and surge forecast values for specific locations. A
general concern should be for the possibility of at least widespread
damage somewhere within Guam and the Northern Marianas. A Flood
Watch is also likely for the Marianas.
properties.instruction:
Stay calm and keep informed. Comply with any evacuation orders that
are issued for your area. If you live in a metal roof or container
home, or you live in a surge zone or any location prone to flooding,
evacuate to a designated shelter or ride out the storm in the sturdy
home of family or friends outside of evacuation zones.

Items to bring to a shelter include a first aid kit, medicines
and prescriptions, baby food and diapers, games and books,
toiletries, a battery powered radio, a cell phone, flashlights
with extra batteries, a blanket or sleeping bag for each person,
personal identification, copies of key papers such as insurance
policies, available cash and credit cards. Remember, pets are not
allowed in most public shelters, so check ahead with your intended
shelter.

Regarding your home or business, cover all windows and doors with
shutters or plywood. Move patio furniture and other loose objects
indoors. Brace all exterior doors, including garage doors. Do
this as early as possible.

If you need to make a trip to the hardware store, the grocery
store, or the gas station, do so as early as possible.

properties.areaDesc: Glasscock, TX; Howard, TX; Mitchell, TX; Scurry, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 15 at 12:38AM CDT until October 15 at 2:30AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 1238 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Big Spring, Snyder, Colorado City, Coahoma, Loraine, Forsan, Lake
Colorado City, Lake Colorado City State Park, Colorado City
Airport, Champion Creek Reservoir, Sand Springs, Inadale,
Westbrook, Cuthbert, Buford, Ira, Dunn, Knapp and Winston Field.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law

properties.areaDesc: Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 12:09PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Depression 29W is located 555 miles northeast of Chuuk,
moving northwest at 13 mph. A turn more to the west is expected to
occur over the next 24 hours. As 29W continues it's journey to the
Marianas, rapid intensification is possible. This would result in
increased west to southwest monsoon flow will increase. This will
allow for showers to increase in coverage any intensity, with locally
heavy rainfall likely.

At this time, 2 to 4 inches of rainfall may develop, with locally
higher amounts possible. If 29W can intensify a little faster than
anticipated, or if it takes a due west track, this could open door
for isolated wind gusts to 30 to 35 knots to develop. Seas currently
look to increase 1 to 3 feet, topping out near 7 feet, but again,
this could be higher if 29W tracks closer to Chuuk or strengthens
faster.

Folks with intra-island travel should delay any travel for a few
days until the developing tropical depression has passed.

* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with

foothills of the Santa Ana mountains. For the Heat Advisory,
temperatures up to 94 expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Inland Areas.

Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Moderate to locally major HeatRisk. Those sensitive to heat may be
impacted.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 9:39AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Tropical Depression 29W continues to organize as it continues
it's long voyage towards the Marianas, and is currently located at
10.6N 160.1E, which is 1030 miles east of Guam. Movement has been
to the northwest at 13 mph, and a more gradual turn to the west-
northwest is expected. It's important for folks to keep in mind
that wobbles in the track occur all the time, and a slight change
can make a big difference in terms of who experiences what, and
for how long.

The main theme we've been telling folks is tropical storm-force
winds look probable over some locations of the Marianas between
Guam and Saipan, with typhoon conditions also possible. Heavy
rainfall will also accompany the storm. Rainfall amounts of 5 to
10 inches, with locally higher amounts possible. For our mariners,
seas will rapidly build Saturday into Sunday, with seas likely
climbing above 20 feet. Some coastal inundation is likely.

For more information on Tropical Depression 29W, please refer to
the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National
Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM and the Tropical
Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under
WMO header WTPN32 PGTW.

...A FIRE WEATHER WATCH IS IN EFFECT FROM FRIDAY MORNING THROUGH

RELATIVE HUMIDITY, AND CRITICALLY DRY FUELS FOR PORTIONS OF
SOUTHEAST ARKANSAS, NORTHWEST LOUISIANA, AND MUCH OF CENTRAL
MISSISSIPPI...

The National Weather Service in Jackson has issued a Fire

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 14 at 2:14PM CDT until October 17 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL AND
SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.With the ongoing drought conditions, we have KBDI values well into
the 700s, with 10-hour and 100-hour fuel moisture values hovering
around 25%. Subsidence behind the front will further dry out the
already dry continental air mass, leading to a significant drop in
dew points following the front. The forecast drops RH values below
30% across central Louisiana and the interior portions of
southeast Texas. Friday through Sunday look to be concerning for
fire weather. However, Saturday appears to be the most critical
day as the dry, subsided airmass becomes fully entrenched over the
highly dried out fuels. This setup is similar to the weather
conditions that sparked the Tiger Island fire in 2023, and fires
that do spark could quickly spread out of control..

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for high winds and low relative humidity, which is
in effect from Friday morning through late Friday night.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 031 Allen, Fire
Weather Zone 032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 033 St. Landry,
Fire Weather Zone 044 Lafayette, Fire Weather Zone 045 Upper
St. Martin, Fire Weather Zone 141 Northern Calcasieu, Fire
Weather Zone 142 Northern Jefferson Davis, Fire Weather Zone
143 Northern Acadia, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire Weather
Zone 201 Hardin, Fire Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper, Fire
Weather Zone 260 Northern Newton, Fire Weather Zone 261
Southern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern Newton.

* TIMING...From Friday morning through late Friday night.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 35 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 87.

* LIGHTNING...

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 3:09AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W has been upgraded to Tropical Depression 29W, and is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 9.6N 161.2E. 29W will
continue to develop and strengthen just north of the region, and will
generally head towards the Marianas. Convergent fresh to strong
westerlies south of 29W's center are producing bands of scattered to
numerous showers capable of strong gusts and locally heavy rainfall,
across Pohnpei and their coastal waters, and Gusty winds across
Kosrae and their costal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests
rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei
through late Friday night as 29W strengthens and passes north of the
island. Gusts to 30 knots will be possible near heavier showers.
Moderate to strong winds with gusts to near-gale for Kosrae through
this afternoon as conditions start to ease there.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
For more information on TD 29W, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

Winds will be particularly hazardous at higher elevations where the
strongest winds are likely to occur. Be especially careful driving in
these mountainous areas. People driving high-profile vehicles should
strongly consider postponing travel in these areas until the winds
subside.

Delay travel through Guadalupe Pass or find another route, if
possible.

NWSheadline: HIGH WIND WATCH IN EFFECT FROM THURSDAY EVENING THROUGH SATURDAY AFTERNOON, ESPECIALLY THROUGH GUADALUPE PASS

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will fall below 6.5 ft after
the Thursday high tide. A south swell from 190 degrees of 3 ft
with a 15 to 17 second period will be present through
Thursday. A moderate period, persistent south swell from 190
will continue into next week.
properties.instruction:
A beach hazards statement for minor tidal overflow means that
high astronomical tides possibly in combination with above normal
surf will likely produce minor flooding of low-lying areas along
the beach such as beach parking lots. Coastal officials should
take the necessary precautionary measures to safeguard their
beaches.

A beach hazards statement is issued when threats such as rip
currents and other hazards are possible.  Caution should be used
when in or near the water.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 14 at 4:17PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "High" for development by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center, and is the subject of a Tropical Cyclone
Formation Alert, meaning development into a significant tropical
cyclone (a tropical depression) is expected within 24 hours. 96W is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 8.7N 160.7E, and
continues to develop and strengthen just north of the region.
Convergent fresh to strong westerlies south of 96W's center are
producing bands of scattered to numerous showers capable of strong
gusts and locally heavy rainfall, across Kosrae, Pohnpei, and their
adjacent coastal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests rainfall
amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei through late
Friday night as 96W strengthens and passes north of the island, with
an additional 1 to 2 inches possible for Kosrae through early
Thursday morning as conditions start to ease there. Gusts to 30 knots
will be possible near heavier showers.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
Keep up to date with the latest information from the National Weather
Service in Tiyan, Guam, and your local emergency management.

NWSheadline: LOCALLY HEAVY RAINFALL AND GUSTY WINDS THROUGH THURSDAY NIGHT AS INVEST 96W PASSES TO THE NORTH

properties.areaDesc: Guam, GU; Rota, MP; Saipan, MP; Tinian, MP
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 13 at 5:31PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend.

This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible.

As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later this weekend.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.
